idiom_name: Promise kept in a Map with a rejection timer
implementation_notes: A promise is the reply channel and a Map keyed by correlation id is the correlation table: the caller stores resolve/reject plus a timer under a fresh id, publishes the request with that id, and the reply handler (an exclusive reply queue or one socket reader) resolves the matching entry. The classic callback/reply-queue structure remains only as the publish options (correlationId, replyTo) and the deadline timer. On a broker, amqplib's RPC tutorial uses an exclusive callback queue or RabbitMQ's amq.rabbitmq.reply-to pseudo-queue; over WebSockets, socket.io's acknowledgement callback or emitWithAck (with ackTimeout) is the same exchange.
pitfalls: Node timers keep the process alive and fire after the promise settled: clearTimeout on every completion path or a long-running process accumulates dead timers and late rejections.
Match before parsing: unknown or duplicate correlation ids must be dropped, never resolved, or a late reply can satisfy a reused entry.
JSON.parse on an unvalidated reply body is a denial-of-service and injection surface; validate the shape before use.

variants.name: amqplib RPC over an exclusive reply queue or direct reply-to
variants.implementation_notes: amqplib exposes the AMQP primitives the pattern needs - publish with replyTo and correlationId, consume the reply queue - as in the library's RPC tutorial: the client declares an exclusive, auto-delete callback queue (or addresses RabbitMQ's amq.rabbitmq.reply-to pseudo-queue, which needs no queue at all) and a single consumer dispatches each reply to the pending entry by correlationId. Use the pseudo-queue for one-shot RPC on the requesting channel and the exclusive queue when replies must survive channel churn.
pitfalls: RabbitMQ's direct reply-to pseudo-queue requires the consumer to be on the same channel that sent the request; otherwise the broker rejects the use.
The consumer must be cancelled and the reply queue deleted when the call completes, or every RPC leaves a consumer behind.
